issue.title: New settings page listing upcoming booking reminders
issue.body:
Harness test (new screen). Add a new page under Settings where users see the reminder emails scheduled for their upcoming bookings (booking title, attendee, send time), read-only. Empty state when there are none.

Details from @lucasgrocha (comment 6756289657):
1. Compute the send time with a fixed rule: 24 hours before the booking start. No new scheduler or schema change.
2. Organizer only: bookings where the user is the host.

Details from @lucasgrocha (comment 6756838767):
1. Accepted bookings only; leave PENDING out.
2. No loading.tsx skeleton.

pm.summary: New read-only Settings page listing reminder emails for the user's upcoming accepted hosted bookings; it is a new screen, so it goes to the Designer next. No open questions.
acceptance_criteria: A new page is reachable from the Settings navigation and shows a list of scheduled booking reminders.
Each row shows booking title, attendee, and reminder send time.
Send time is computed as exactly 24 hours before the booking start time, with no new scheduler or schema change.
Only upcoming bookings (start time in the future) are listed.
Only bookings where the signed-in user is the host/organizer are listed; bookings where they are only an attendee are excluded.
Only ACCEPTED bookings are listed; PENDING (and other statuses) are excluded.
When there are no matching bookings, an empty state is shown.
The page is read-only: no edit, delete or create actions.
No loading.tsx skeleton is added for the page.
Another user's bookings are never shown; unauthenticated access is redirected as for other Settings pages.
User-facing strings are added to the English locale file.
Changes stay within the allowed scope, with no schema, lockfile or dependency changes.

research.summary: Research done: the closest pattern is the push-notifications settings page. A server page needs a nav entry, a view, a new query for hosted accepted bookings, and en strings. Ready for the plan.
patterns: Settings pages live at apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/settings/(settings-layout)/my-account/<slug>/page.tsx. They export generateMetadata via _generateMetadata(t(title), t(description), undefined, undefined, path) and render a view from apps/web/modules/settings/my-account/<slug>-view.tsx using the ~/settings/... alias.

Auth in server pages (general/page.tsx): getServerSession({ req: buildLegacyRequest(await headers(), await cookies()) }), then redirect to /auth/login?callbackUrl=<path> when there is no user id. Data comes via createRouterCaller or a server fetch and is passed to a client view as props. This fits the 'no loading.tsx' rule.
Nav entry: add a child to the my_account tabs in SettingsLayoutAppDirClient.tsx (name key, href, trackingMetadata { section: 'my_account', page }), next to push_notifications.
Strings go in packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json as snake_case keys (e.g. push_notifications). The nav name and the page title/description use the same key convention. Only English is edited.

Data: no existing 'upcoming hosted accepted bookings' query was confirmed. get.handler.ts only has bookings filters, which are not guaranteed to cover this case. The BookingRepository in packages/features/bookings/repositories has many find* methods with Prisma queries using BookingStatus.ACCEPTED. A new narrow repository method (userId = host, status ACCEPTED, startTime > now, select title, startTime, attendees) is the likely shape. The planner must decide between this and a tRPC route; avoid schema changes.

Send time = startTime minus 24h, computed in a small pure helper, e.g. in packages/lib/, so it can be unit-tested. Format dates with existing helpers/useLocale (see packages/lib/dateTimeFormatter.ts).
Read-only list with an empty state. Look for an existing EmptyScreen in @calcom/ui/components/empty-screen and use it. No loading.tsx.

Human-review paths in scope: packages/features/bookings/lib/, packages/features/auth/, packages/lib/server/. Place new code outside them (e.g. packages/features/bookings/repositories/ or packages/lib/) where possible.
test_commands: TZ=UTC yarn vitest run <path-to-new-test-file>  (root script: "test": "TZ=UTC vitest run")
yarn type-check  (turbo run type-check; CI uses yarn type-check:ci)

design_need.summary: This is a new read-only Settings screen, so it needs design before the plan. Brief written for the Designer covering the list rows and the empty state.
design_need.design_brief:
Design a new read-only Settings page, "Booking reminders", under My Account in Settings, placed next to Push notifications in the settings navigation.

Purpose: users see the reminder emails scheduled for their upcoming bookings.

Content rules (already decided, do not reopen):
- Only upcoming, ACCEPTED bookings where the user is the host. PENDING is excluded.
- Each row shows: booking title, attendee, and reminder send time.
- Send time is the booking start minus 24 hours.
- Read-only: no edit, delete, create or toggle actions.
- No loading skeleton state. The page renders with data on first paint.

Needed from the Designer:
1. Page layout: title and description header consistent with other My Account settings pages (e.g. push notifications, out of office). Use existing @calcom/ui components and tokens.
2. List or table layout for rows: booking title, attendee, send time. Specify column or field order, how multiple attendees are shown (e.g. first name plus "+N", or a list), and how long titles truncate.
3. Date and time formatting: send time in the user's timezone and locale, with date and time shown clearly. Say whether the booking start is also shown as secondary context (optional).
4. Empty state: use the existing EmptyScreen pattern, with icon, headline and short explanatory text. No call to action, since the page is read-only.
5. Responsive behavior for mobile and desktop widths, and the accessibility basics: semantic table or list, headings, contrast.
6. Copy: proposed English strings for the nav label, page title, page description, column labels and empty state, in snake_case key form for common.json.

Out of scope: a loading skeleton, filtering, pagination decisions beyond a sensible default (note one if the list could be long), and any scheduler or settings controls.
